pinterest.title: 15 Engagement Ring Styles and Who Each One Suits, From Solitaire to Toi et Moi
pinterest.description: Shortlisting engagement ring styles? Our guide puts 15 types of engagement rings through four lenses: personality, everyday life, how the ring sits on the hand, and how it travels and photographs at a wedding abroad. Solitaire, halo, hidden halo, three-stone, toi et moi, east-west, cluster, art deco, bezel style, eternity-style, coloured gemstone centres and more, each with a suits you if and a think twice if line.

pinterest.title: Halo Engagement Ring: Who It Suits and What to Know Before You Choose
pinterest.description: A halo engagement ring frames the centre stone with smaller stones, adding sparkle and making the centre look as large as the halo itself. It suits sparkle lovers who enjoy a ring that is noticed across a dinner table. Think twice if the wearer works with their hands: many small stones mean more upkeep, so book a jeweller check every six months, or at least yearly, and check it before you fly.

pinterest.title: Toi et Moi Engagement Ring: Two Stones, One Story
pinterest.description: French for "you and me", a toi et moi engagement ring sets two stones side by side, said to symbolise two lives intertwining. The idea is old: in 1796 Napoleon gave Josephine a sapphire and diamond toi et moi. It suits couples who want a ring that is plainly about two people. Plan the wedding band early, book periodic checks, and keep an eye on both stones during pool and beach days.

slides: 15 engagement ring styles. The real question is which one suits the person wearing it.
Four lenses for every ring: personality, everyday life, how it sits on the hand, and how it travels and photographs at a wedding abroad.
Minimal taste, active life? A solitaire kept low, or a bezel style with a smooth rim that rarely snags.
Sparkle first? Halo, pavé or cluster. Many small stones, so book a jeweller check every six months, or at least yearly.
Sentimental, or planning a surprise? Three-stone or toi et moi. GIA says three-stone suits almost any hand.
Design-led? East-west, art deco or bypass. Try any wedding band alongside before you order.
Off to a wedding abroad? Ring in your carry-on, off before chlorinated pools, and a plain band for snorkelling and boat days.
Shortlisted two or three styles? Tell us your rough date and chat with a Wedded Advisor about the wedding abroad that comes next.
instagram_carousel.caption:
Most ring galleries name a look and stop there. Our new guide asks who each look actually suits.

We put 15 engagement ring styles through four lenses: personality, everyday life, how the ring sits on the hand, and how it travels and photographs at a wedding abroad. Every style gets a plain description, a "suits you if" line and a "think twice if" line.

A few things worth knowing before you sit down with a jeweller:
Choose the overall style first and the setting second. GIA treats the look of a ring and the way its stone is held as two different things.
Halo, pavé and cluster designs rely on many small stones, so book a check every six months, or at least yearly.
Not sure of the wearer's hand? A round or princess centre, or a three-stone layout, suits almost any finger.
A hidden halo or split shank shows its detail side-on, so brief your photographer.

Travelling for the wedding? Pack the ring in your carry-on, take it off before chlorinated pools, and tell your insurer your travel dates.

The full guide is linked in bio.
